record.tranche_reason: Tests whether a different explicit regularizer, shake-shake, changes test error and overfitting in image classifiers.
record.gate_note: The paper tests shake-shake regularization and branch-correlation measurements. It does not test the specific methods or properties in V1–V8. Figure-only training and test curves are not transcribed as numerical rows.
record.test_reason: Section 2.2 reports an additional result bearing on V5: with the CIFAR-100 training recipe held at 1800 epochs, reducing batch size from 128 to 32 was necessary for competitive E-E-B performance. The shake-shake comparisons themselves do not test V1–V8.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate: the authors conclude that shake-shake can combat overfitting, suggest branch decorrelation as an explanation, report strong CIFAR results, and leave the exact dynamics unresolved.
record.recipe_differences: Uses stochastic affine combinations of residual branches rather than the interventions or measurements in the claim versions; trains for 1800 epochs with data augmentation and cosine learning-rate annealing.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported results vary with forward/backward coefficient updates, batch versus image level, architecture, batch size, and coefficient interval. The authors report that S-S-I underfits on architecture A, regularization no longer works on architecture B, and wider coefficient intervals can cause divergence without Batch Normalization.

fits_no_version.finding: Stochastic branch mixing lowers test error in several settings, including 4.27% to 3.47% on CIFAR-10 and 16.34% to 15.85% on CIFAR-100.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Stochastic affine mixing of residual branches can lower image-classification test error.

fits_no_version.finding: Benefits depend on architecture and coefficient range: architecture B gains essentially nothing, architecture A can underfit, and architecture C can diverge.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Shake-shake regularization requires architecture-dependent control of regularization strength.

fits_no_version.finding: Shake-shake models appear to have lower correlation between residual branch outputs.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Shake-shake regularization is associated with branch-output decorrelation.

record.problems: The CIFAR-100 comparison uses few tests (2 baseline runs, 3 shake-even runs, and 1 shake-shake run). Several architecture variants were tested once or twice. Branch correlation results are shown in a figure without numeric values in the text. Training and test curves are shown in figures without transcribed numerical values.
record.rows_left_out: Table 1 contains additional coefficient-update and width combinations, including Shake-Keep conditions. Not extracted because table cell alignment for the remaining values is ambiguous in the supplied flattened text; the paper's textual summary says Shake-Keep has no particularly strong effect and image-level coefficients seem to improve regularization.

untested.parts: Random-label fitting and its comparison with natural-label held-out accuracy.
Width beyond the width required for zero training error; the width comparisons do not establish interpolation.
Convolutional versus fully connected networks and the contribution of local connectivity.
Adaptive optimizers versus SGD and optimizer-tuning conditions.
Penalty magnitude, a batch-size threshold or sweep, language models, and whether longer training or recipe adaptations recover larger-batch performance.
Dropout interventions, small-data effects, excessive dropout, and jointly removing dropout and weight decay.
Magnitude-aware weight perturbations and their ranking of generalization gaps.
Identifying and removing memorized examples versus random removals.

missing.what: Record the qualitative batch-size comparison: CIFAR-100 E-E-B performance is described as uncompetitive at batch size 128, requiring reduction to 32 under the 1800-epoch recipe. The smaller-batch baseline error is 16.34%; the larger-batch error and run count are unstated.
missing.locator: Section 2.2, paragraph following Table 2; training duration in the preceding implementation description.

record.verdict_notes: The record's blanket not-tested judgment overlooks the qualitative batch-size result. That result provides narrow support for V5; the main shake-shake results support a different claim. No verdict is inferred from width alone, dropout analogies, or branch correlations.

versions.untested_parts: Convolutional versus fully connected networks and local connectivity.
Large-batch effects under fixed epoch budgets and recipe adaptations.
Dropout effects and removing dropout with weight decay.
Magnitude-aware sharpness and its relation to the generalization gap.
Removing memorized examples and measuring test accuracy.

relationships.condition: CIFAR-100 E-E-B ResNeXt, two GPUs, 1800 epochs, batch size 128 versus 32.
relationships.reason: Based on section 2.2 rather than an extracted row: the authors report that batch size must fall from 128 to 32 for competitive baseline performance. No larger-batch error value is supplied.
relationships.display_finding: The study reports that reducing batch size was necessary for competitive baseline accuracy, but this result has not been verified. The larger-batch error was unavailable.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.
